To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified and characterized a Na+/b bile acid transporter from rat liver and that the transporter is expressed in various mammalian tissues.
we have isolated a cDNA encoding the hepatocyte Na/bile acid cotransporter, which we have functionally expressed in Xenopus oocytes, and we have characterized its properties.
the cloned transporter is a sodium-dependent transporter for bile acids, which is highly expressed in liver and kidney, and is also expressed at lower levels in the intestine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular cloning and functional expression of the rat liver Na+/bile-acid cotransporter.
the molecular characterization of the hepatobiliary Na+/bile-acid transport system.
the molecular cloning and characterization of a novel Na(+)-dependent bile acid transporter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cloned transporter is responsible for the Na+-dependent uptake of bile acids in liver cells and that the cloned transporter might also be responsible for the uptake of bile acids from the intestine and from the kidney.
the cloned cDNA encodes the hepatocyte sodium-dependent bile acid cotransport protein, which is a glycoprotein with an apparent molecular mass in the range of 33-40 kDa.
the cloned cDNA encodes the hepatocyte Na+-dependent bile acid transport system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned the first member of a new family of transport proteins that are responsible for the uptake of organic compounds from the circulation.
the cDNA for the Na(+)-dependent bile acid uptake system in the liver has been cloned.
we have cloned a transporter for bile acids that is expressed in liver, intestine, and kidney, and that is involved in the absorption of endogenous and dietary bile acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cloned transporter is highly conserved among mammals and that it is expressed in various organs.
we have identified the first mammalian transporter for the uptake of bile acids.
we have identified a new family of transporters, the Na(+)-dependent bile acid cotransporters, that are expressed in liver, intestine, and kidney.
